chapter: Chicago, the Woodside, the army and 52nd Street
title: Rehearsals without a piano; Clyde Hart joins; Prez's pride and shyness
summary: They played a few jobs and recorded with Una Mae Carlisle; Prez quit jobs that did not suit him but was shy offstage.

story.theme_name: Lester Young: the man, the sound, the Basie years
story.community_name: Remembering Lester Young: Prez the man and his sound

blocks.x: But any way, I told you rehearsed -- we rehearsed and we didn't have a piano player. We played these jobs. And during this time we recorded for Una Mae Carlisle, (unintelligible) I will

some very good things with her. But I got Clyde Hart to come down to rehearsal, and Clyde started playing with us, so we played around for awhile until there was -- there wasn't very much work during that time any way, you know, and Lester would quit the job if it didn't suit him. You know, money or no money, he was a very proud man, and had funny ways -- you could just hurt his feelings. And he would just walk off, and quit, you know.
He wasn't a terribly gregarious person, was he?

No you had to know him. You had to know him for him to open up to you. You know,he was a very -- actually he was very shy, every way but musically;he was very outgoing musically. But this was a very good experience. Now, while we were rehearsing Lionel brought his first band to New York, and this is the first time I met Lee Young, Prez' brother. They came down, and let's see, Lee Young, Sir Charles Thompson. What is the bass player's name in -- Vernon Alley and Ray Perry, from Boston, played saxophone and played violin. Tremendous musician. And who else was in the band? Dexter Gordon was in the band. And I think Illinois Jacquet was in the band. They had quite a band. It was quite a band.
